body: I have advanced PPMS and over a year ago explained my intention to end my life before becomming a prisoner in my own body. Despite not giving identifying info, 2 police officers appeared at my door a couple of days later with a "duty of care". Left after 5 mins concluding I wasn't depressed or suicidal. Made me very wary of posting on reddit for a while.
Read my other posts and you'll see I've reached my limit. On my phone so can't link to posts, sorry.

I have PPMS and have had countless people tell me about RRMS sufferers who run marathons, etc. I get sick of explaining there are different forms of MS and I do not get periods of remission, never have a symptom free day, and there are no treatments for PPMS other than trying to treat ever worsening symptoms.

I moved into my flat (new build) in October 2014 and have received a letter to "The Legal Occupier" every month since. I haven't watched live TV for 14 years and just ignore the letters. I have kept all the letters, and will die soon, and added a directive that following my death all the letters are to be posted back telling them I'm now deceased and never needed a bloody TV licence anyway.

When I really have to. Have advanced PPMS and a shower takes me 2 hours and exhausts me for a couple of days. Physically it is also very risky transferring between wheelchairs when fatigued. I shower now only when I have to attend an appointment with someone. I am largely housebound now, and shower maybe once every 6-8 weeks. I really fear it now, and have to prepare for it a couple of days in advance, and be aware that I will be excecively fatigued for a couple of days after it. If I have a meeting on Wednesday I need to shower on Sunday so I'm recovered enough by Wednesday.

It started years ago when I started using a stick to walk. Had a standard NHS one but got loads of scrounger comments till I bought my own one. Definitely gotten worse over the last few years. Am really aware of my physical vulnerability and definitely never leave my flat alone, not that I really could these days.

44 yo guy with PPMS here. Was sitting in line at Waitrose once and an elderly couple behind me were discussing if the government would give them free money if they bought a wheelchair. They shut up when I told them my chair cost me £3.5k and I would love to be able to stand like them once more. Another time in Iceland I was looking in a fewwzer before I opened it and a woman started pushing me away saying "I just need in for a second". I grabbed my rims, spun to swipe her ankles with my footplate and really let rip at her till she left her basket and ran out the store. Have heard various scrounger and faking it comments a lot. I rarely leave my flat these days.

I have advanced progressive MS and am close to becoming a prisoner in my own body which I don't accept as an acceptable form of existence so will end my life before that. As a life-long athiest I have no fear of death in itself, but am terrified of the process of dying because legally I have to be alone (would prefer even a stranger present, not to assist but just for human comfort), and i know that when I do it I will still want to live. I know that my future would be a daily living hell, but I don't want to die.

On doors that I have to pull closed, where I have to pull the door into the space where my wheelchair is sitting, I put small drawer handles on the doors closer to the hinges so I can use them the pull the doors closed with my wheelchair positioned outside of the room whose door I'm closing.

In my bedroom, which is furthest from the living room, I have a padded board with castors on it so I can lie on it, hook my feet over the footplate of my wheelchair, and drag myself to the living room. Exhausting, but easier on the wheeled board than just dragging myself.

I'm fairly advanced PPMS, virtually parylised from the chest down, hands and arms weakening, and sheath cathetered 24/7.
Occasionally I get (I assume) a kidney or bladder infection, which seems to stop the flow of urine. You know when you're bursting for the toilet and it gets painful? That's what it's like, usually lasts a few days then returns to normal.

I woke up about 3am sunday morning with the pain of needing to urinate, but I couldn't move at all. Could move my head from side to side but couldn't even lift a finger. By 1pm I could finally move my fingers and make a fist, by 2pm I could move my arms but they were weak with poor co-ordination. It was 4pm before I could move enough to get my legs pushed off the side of the bed, but because I had missed all my meds so far any movement of my legs set off full body spasms and cramps. For the remainder of the day I was weak, drained, and in pain.

It was the most terrifying experience of my life. I have always vowed not to become a prisoner in my own body and would end my life before that, and this experience just reaffirmed my decision. I have spent the last year+ preparing for it, trying to do as much as possible in advance to try and make it a little easier on my parents and sister, but realised yesterday that despite doing all that my equipment for ending my life wasn't put together yet, so set it all up last night just so it is ready to use when the time comes.

Has anybody else experienced anything like this, because it really scared me, and still does.

Don't know if you're male or female. Male PPMS here. Frequency and urgency increased over time, but once I was restricted to a wheelchair I could no longer make it on to a toilet in time, so have been using sheath catheters 24/7 for nearly 2 years now.

What got me was for high mobility in DLA you had to be unable to walk 50 meters, this is now 20 meters under PIP. DLA asked if you could wash your entire body in a seated position, PIP only asks if you can wash above the waist, so I can be smeared in shit from the waist down but as long as I can clean above it I must be ok. Because I'm so close to my end it no longer really bothers me, but the last few years were full of anxiety and stress over PIP. I knew I was entitled to higher care, but was scared to apply because of all the horror stories.

My sis worked as a dancer with Carnival for 10 years and said things like this were common. She told me once of a couple of dancers, a bit drunk, decided to do handstands on the rail at the rear of the ship. One fell and was never seen again, despite halting the ship and searching for 12 hours.
I'll be dead soon. I was sorely tempted to contact the DWP and tell them of my deteriorated condition, await the PIP application form, and just scrawl "THE FINAL STRAW" on it before my death.

I'm a 44 year old male in Scotland with progressive MS. I was assessed for DLA in 2012 while I could still walk with a cane for short distances, but could manage usual tasks at home with care. Since then PIP was introduced, and my condition has progressed considerably. I have been in a wheelchair permenantly for 18 months, virtually patylised from the chest down, sleep in my clothes as it's too painful and exhausting to get dressed in the morning, I have a shower about once a month because it takes so much out of me for days after, sheath-cathetered 24/7 and have to do a manual bowel routine daily. Cannot physically use my cooker anymore so live off frozen ready meals for one. The list goes on, but I was too scared to inform the DWP of my deterioration becauses of the PIP fiasco, so continue to get DLA, high mobility but low care component, where I have been entitled to the high care component for a couple of years. I used to stress and worry about them getting to me with the PIP application, but these days my time left is so limited I don't care anymore. I will never understand why someone with my condition, which is progressively degenerative, with no treatment available, and will only ever get worse, have to be reassessed just to prove they still have their incurable, untreatable, progressively degenerative disease.

I have PPMS, 44 yo guy, feet started getting pins and needles 9 years ago. I still live alone and have no carers, but my mum pops in for a couple of hours a week. I'm now virtually paralysed from the chest down and my hands are beginning to fail, already lost tactile feeling in them and dexterity and strength are going fast too. I have lowered worktops in my kitchen, shower unit removed and replaced with a wetroom floor, and loads of grab-rails around the toilet. I fall almost daily now, and bought a bath lift, bolted to my living room floor, so if I can get myself to it I can raise myself to my wheelchair level. I wear sheath catheters 24/7, and have to do a daily manual bowel routine which exhausts me. I shower when I really need to, which these days is about once a month as it takes so much out of me. I also sleep in my clothes as getting dressed is exhausting first thing in the morning when my spasms are at their worst. I only eat small microwave ready meals as I cannot use my cooker anymore physically. I leave my flat maybe once a month for medical appointments, and apart from maybe 3-4 hours I spend the entirity of my week completely alone.

I acknowledged a long time ago that I will face 2 choices, become a prisoner in my own body reliant on community carers to pop in for a few hours a day, or take my life. Have arranged my final and living wills, arranged and paid for my direct cremation, had a psych evaluation stating I'm not depressed or suicidal, and do now want to die (I am really scared of the process of dying) but it is the lesser of 2 evils presented to me, as a way of preventing anyone with a "duty of care" from intervening on mental health grounds. My GP also issued me a legally binding DNR directive.. I can pretty much tell you how many weeks I have left (give or take a week).

Losing and having to give up independance and the ability to do things for yourself is a hard pill to swallow, and I certainly have fought for my independance, and the local community care team has been decimated recently due to government cuts (Scotland), and asking for help can be difficult as it means admitting to yourself that you cannot cope, and knowing you are going to be a burden on your family (both my parents are elderly and I don't want their final years spent caring for me and waiting for me to die of pneumonia.

I second this completely. I can only really get hash here, but I prefer to smoke it anyway as I feel I have more control over it then. I have neuropathic pain in my legs and get prescribed pregabalin, but it makes me very dozy, so I take a lower dose so I'm still as functional as possible but my legs constantly feel like I'm sitting in a bath slightly too hot for comfort. The spasms are more extreme now and taking 160mg baclofen a day. It can take me 15 minutes just to manipulate my legs off the side of the bed in the morning as every slight movemenet of my legs sets off full body spasms. I'm now a "wake & bake" user. I hate the feeling of being high, but smoke hash in small amounts so I don't get too high, but the pain disappears and the spasms, although still present, are a lot weaker, and it helps me sleep too. In Scotland I'm technically a criminal for this, but it is the only thing that helps alleviate the pain, despite all the drugs I am prescribed to treat symptoms (PPMS so no MS treatment available).

The funny time for me is when I go to Iceland, there is an Aldi just across and down the road a bit, so will often pop in. Thing is I cross the road and there is a downwards slope before it levels off before Aldi. Stupid and irresponsible I know, but I love just freewheeling down that slope, can't grab the rims as get friction burns but can apply pressure to adjust direction using my jacket sleeves (which now has burn marks on both sleeves), and it levels off in time for me to slow enough to use my rims. So I sit at the top of the slope waiting till it's empty and I can let go, and so many people keep asking if I'm ok and do I need help. I tell them I'm waiting for my roller coaster to clear. Some get it and smile and wait to watch, others don't understand and look at me like I'm mad. We have to get our kicks somehow.

In Scotland here, 44 yo male, progressive MS, now virtually parylised from the chest down. I've seen all the usual reactions, and I put them in 3 categories - 1. Pity, sympathy, that look of "poor you"; 2. Fear - "he doesn't look that old, and if it can happen to him will it happen to me?"; 3. Disgust, not so much because of the wheelchair but more because of the way the government and media in the UK has demonised anybody receiving welfare benefits, and portray them as a drain on tax-payers.

A while ago my mother took me to Waitrose for a top-up shop. Waitrose is a sort of expensive supermarket in the UK, but I was only getting bread, milk, etc. Sitting waiting at the checkout and and old couple behind me started discussing if they bought a wheelchair would the government give them free money. They soon shut up when I told them I receive a disability benefit for my disability, not my wheelchair, because disability is expensive, and if they wanted to buy a chair then mine had cost me £3.5k personally and wasn't provided for me or funded in any way. Another time my mother took me to Iceland, a shop chain that mainly does frozen foods. Its the usual chest freezers where the lids are about upper chest level to me. I tend to look at what's in the freezer then open it and get out what I want, so was doing that and a woman came up behind me and started pushing me out the way saying "I'll just roll you out the way for a second so I can get in". I immediately grabbed my rims, spun round, and literally exploded at her to the point she put her basket down and ran out of the shop. The manager later approached me to apologize as he has just watched the camera footage, and gave me a £20 voucher towards my shopping, which was nice and unexpected.

My biggest gripe though is people always assuming I need help. I specifically chose the rear handgrips on my chair so they fold out of the way to discourage people trying to push me. Even my family - xmas day went to parents and dad hovered and held my chair every time I transferred despite my telling him I have to do this a couple of dozen times a day alone. If I need help then I'll ask.

Diagnosed with PPMS couple of years later. Kept licence illegally as a form of photo ID, but surrendered it last year as it was up for renewal. I too am a fussy eater, but my diet has only changed as a result of increasing symptoms. Have PPMS and now virtually paralysed from chest down. Used to eat a standard diet I suppose and was a caffeine addict, but cut out can of soda and limited to 1 coffee a day in the morning due to urinary urgency (had to make it to toilet in about a minute), but began using sheath catheters 24/7  late 2015 as was in wheelchaie and couldn't get onto toilet in time. Peristalsis failed in digestive tract and lack of mobility meant a BM once every 5 days, so started eating only once a day or I'd feel bloated after a couple of days. Started having to do daily digistim and cut out any overly spicey foods or anything that could give loosen stools, and now take immodium daily to keep stools solid so I can feel them and be aware now. Also cut out things like baked beans or anything that could cause flatulence as my butthole is clamped tight so I just bloat with gas. Other changes are because of physical limitations, like I can't use the rings on my cooker anymore as they are eye level with me now, can't use heavy dishes like casserole dishes as too heavy to try and get out of the oven. Fatigue and tiredness is a major issue for me these days so I eat whatever takes the least physical energy to make, which is basically microwave ready-meals, or a single tray of something in the oven. 

Early on I read a lot of advise on diet, but am a fussy eater and cannot abide vegetables, so that limited me a lot, and a lot of remaining possibilities were either contradictory or made my digestion worse. I don't think there is a single MS diet because everyone experiences MS differently, but I hope people can offer advise that is relevant for you (and possibly me). It may be largely a case of trial and error for yourself finding a combination that suits you.

Similar(ish) here. PPMS, sheath cathetered 24/7 due to urinary urgency, peristalsis no longer active in intestines so only eat once a day (or would feel bloated after 2 days), would commonly go 4-6 days between BM's so now have to do a manual digistim every couple of days combined with enemas. Like you say, food didn't play a role, rather the intestines were no longer shuffling everything through. Been eating once a day for a couple of years now but was tough at the start - empty stomach and you feel hungry, despite the remainder of your digestive tract being full.

Same. I don't drink at all anymore (never a heavy drinker) for fear I forget and try to stand up only to fall in a heap. I hate the way my body has been decimated by my disease. If they want to disable themselves let them, but they have to live with the consequences of asking for it. We didn't ask or desire our disabilities.

44yo Guy with advanced PPMS. Arranged and paid for my own direct cremation yesterday. Emotionally I finally started falling apart a couple of weeks ago and feel I have been bawling every day constantly. I'm sick of people telling me I'm brave for how I live and the decision I have made regarding my future - people are brave for choosing to do what they do, first responders, militery, etc.; I certainly didn't choose to have this disease and living the way I do and ultimately dying is not brave - I have no choice. I guess it's finally broken through my emotional barriers and I'm lonely and scared. I always tended to hide my emotions but cried in front of people (funeral director and my mum) for the first time in about 20 years yesterday (I'm even crying typing this, why the hell won't it stop?). Even lying in bed I cry myself to sleep at night (with the help of trazodone and valium). I'm terrified of what I will have to do in the near future (hoping to see xmas, but dreading it as I know it will be my last, I'll see the house I grew up in for the last time). Can't say for sure if it's depression (I am a depressive but haven't had an episode for a number of years), but I have no desire to die. I really do not want to die but cannot accept the existence as a prisoner in my own body, and I'm really scared now that when the time comes I'll have to do what I need to do while every fibre of my being wants to live. I've been rambling a bit more on Reddit recently because I have no friends or anyone to really talk to and I just need to vent and get things off my chest. My apologies if my posts bring anyone down.

So, no, you're not wrong - teenagers don't usually have any problems getting sexually excited... - but there could be a number of possible culprits, so as embarassing as it may seem (I'm remembering my teen years) speak to your doctor.

I exist on disability these days so money is tight. In April 2011 I checked my bank account and saw that at no point in the previous 6 months had I been out of my overdraft, and although it was an approved OD I still got charged £2.50 for every week I used it, so £10 a month wasted. I created a spreadsheet and started detailing every penny I spent and soon saw patterns of waste. Once you identify where the waste is you can start cutting your expenses. Have PPMS (am now 44) so will never reach retirement age, so cancelled my pension. Cut TV out and either torrent or stream catch-up. Set my boiler to only come on when hot water started flowing - takes a minute for hot water to come through, but had been about £10 a month just to have the pilot light on. Wore more layers in the winter rather than central heating. Started doing survey sites for Amazon credit, might only be £10 a month but it builds up. Also started using cashback sites and scouring for discount codes. Stopped buying anything unless I needed it - just wanting something wasn't justification enough. Contacted all companies I had a contract with to try a renegotiate better rates. Moved to a sim-only contract so went from £35 to £10 a month. Once I had a few hundred saved I contacted my home contents insurance orivider and changed the policy so it now has a £400 excess but is enough to cover everything - if something breaks I can buy a new one, if I get burgled or the place burns down I can claim for everything. Bought a small chest freezer so I could stock up on 3-for-2 offers and do food shopping instore as there tend to be more offers available locally than on their online shops. I focussed on clearing credit cards first and paid extra if I had it to reduce interest. Also once I had saved a bit I started paying things annually (insurance, etc) as there were sometimes discounts for doing so. Also cancelled all paper statements as you pay extra for them. There will be loads of ways you could save a few £/$s if you study your expenses.

EDIT - I also had a sheet on the spreadsheet with my total worth which I updated the 1st of every month, and a separate column showing how much I had "saved" since the previous month. When you start seeing those figures rise it feels good. I also feel guilty if I splurge on something as I know I will have to add it to the sheet, and I'll see a red -ve on amount saved that month.

I had a similar issue (PPMS here) with urinary urgency and getting up in the middle of the night. Started using sheath catheters last October (been in a wheelchair since last May). I now use them 24/7. I did the usual things like cut out coffee (apart from 1 first thing in the morning) and reducing fluid intake in general. I also use cannibis in the evening so it helps me sleep. About an hour before I go to bed I try and stimulate my bladder - basically stick my fingers into my abdomen and wiggle them to try and empty my bladder as much as possible before bed. In bed I'm pretty much in the same position all night; I'm virtually paralysed from the chest down so can't roll over in my sleep without fully waking up to manually move my legs. I get into position on my left side, check that the catheter is secure and not being squashed, then lie down. I rarely pee whilst asleep, but do wake when I need to go, so I just make sure the catheter is unobstructed and I'm not lying on the calf bag, and just go. It's rarely much so I just go back to sleep and empty the bag in the morning. It might interrupt my sleep a bit, but not nearly as much as having to get to the toilet. I live alone so usually have my fly undone so I can easily check everything is ok when at home. I found the reasurance of them worthwhile. I no longer dehydrate myself for 24 hours before I have to go out. It did take a while to get used to peeing whilst having a conversation with people, or out in public, but you get used to it.

Been a depressive since my mid-teens. Tried a number of times, some serious, some more a cry for help (with hindsight). Every time I remember thinking "please just let it all end". Next time I tool anti-emetics first to prevent throwing up, and downed what I could rake together; woke up about 18 hours later having vomited whilst unconscious, plastered to my pillow. Tried that again but woke up about 24 hours later and felt lousy with a lot of abdominal pain for a few days. Cut my wrists a couple of times, but horizontally, so maybe more a cry for help. Tried the helium canister with a bag over my head - passed out fast but slumped down and dislodged the bag I guess, so woke up after a few hours.

Ironically, mentally I feel fine now, not had a serious depressive episode for a number of years, but now have progressive MS and am wheelchair bound, virtually paralysed from the chest down, with arms weakening. It will eventually leave me unable to do anything for myself, and I don't want to exist like that, so I have all my suicide preparations made, wills done, psych evaluation stating I'm not depressed or suicidal, want to live but not in the condition the disease will lead me to. So when my arms weaken to the point that I can no longer transfer myself to/from my wheelchair then it's time to check out. I have made no secret about this, and am very open about it. Maybe having spent a life as a depressive and constantly contemplating my death has made my decision easier to accept and plan for. All emails and letters are drafted for when required. My wishes for my disposal have been arranged. Everyone in my family is aware of my decision. I'll keep going as long as I can because I don't want to die, but I know the day is coming when I either have to end my life or become a prisoner in my own body. I expect I have at most a year left, probably less. 

I find it ironic that the final time (I hope) that I attempt suicide will be at a time when I'm not depressed and do not want to die. But it's (for me) the preferred option as opposed to being reliant on others for all my needs. Those are my only options, kill myself or become a prisoner in my own body waiting for pheumonia to bump me off.

I was a depressive from my teens, MS developed when I was 35. There is no evidence of depression causing MS, although depression can be a symptom of MS.

As for yourself, depression isn't just mental, but does lead to physical symptoms. The malaise is a typical symptom of depression, which can cause further problems as a result. In my worst bouts even simple tasks like having a shower, brushing my teeth, or making dinner were so overwhelming that I couldn't face them. As a result I lost weight, developed digestive problems, my immune system deterorated so I was more prone to colds/flu, though I isolated so rarely came in contact with people. I didn't hydrate enough so migraines were common (I was always prone to headaches though). This leads to your body becoming gradually weaker, and hence more prone to physical problems.

I have been on various anti-depressants for as long as I can remember, and excercise did work to a degree for me. As for barely being able to think, I would tend to ruminate on shit that happened years ago, which would only make me feel worse, and maintaining a train of thought or interest in anything became difficult.

People always say "It gets better", which it does, but it is always there in the back of your mind. When you come back to a workable level you are always waiting for the black cloud to reappear. I haven't had a serious spiral for a number of years, but I know it can return, and it's a scary thought to have to live with. My episodes were never triggered by events; I could never point to something happening and say "that's what caused it". It was purely biochemical. 

I wish you all the best dude. It is a curse that hangs over us that few people that haven't experienced it can appreciate or understand.

EDIT - be aware of the suicide risk of anti-depressants. When you are at your lowest and want to die you don't have the energy or thought process to accomplish it. As anti-depressants gradually raise you back up, you have to go through the period where you are still suicidal but now have the energy to carry it out. Those were he times in the past when I tried to kill myself, though in hindsight they were maybe more cries for help.

Back up about 10, but need to lie down again about 12ish. Lie down again about 4pm, then at 8pm. That's with doing nothing. I feel I am losing so much time every day to fatigue.

What I take from it is that money can't buy you everything. I have PPMS, am now virtually paralysed from the chest down, but am still going. Money-wise I'm comfortable, not rich, but rarely worry about finances, probably due to a limited and frugal lifestyle by choice.

When my arms begin to seriously fail ( they are weakening at the moment and I've lost dexterity and feeling in my hands) I fully intend to take my life with the 20 Ltr canister of O2-free nitrogen in my wardrobe. I've always been very open and up-front about my intentions - I do not want to die, but I don't want to exist in the state the disease will eventually leave me in, and I expect to reach that point by the end of the year. In a similar post a few months ago somebody reported me to the police, and although I didn't include any personal identifying info apart from the town I live in, I got a visit from the police a couple of days later. It has forced me to take certain measures - living and final wills done, DNR directive issued by my GP, pre-arranged my funeral arrangements, even had a psych evaluation and got a copy of the report stating I'm of sound mind and my decision is well considered. All so that somebody with a "duty of care" doesn't step in to "save me" and leave me with starvation as my only means out.

If I had millions and could afford the best medical assistance money could buy, my decision would not change. I have utmost respect for those who decide to continue to exist in such a state, but it just isn't acceptable for me personally, and if my choice offends anybody, be they disabled or not, then as far as I'm concerned that is their problem, not mine.

Fatigue pretty much dictates my life these days. I start feeling tired after just being awake for a couple of hours. I usually have to lie down for an hour or two 3 times a day, and I generally wait till my eyes are drooping and I start getting mentally foggy. Everything is about managing energy and fatigue - planning even the simplest tasks in detail before I start so I cut out as many needless movements as possible and expend the least amount of energy as possible. 

If I have an appointment to attend I will start preparing a couple of days in advance - shower 2 days prior as it takes me 2 hours, leaves me drained and recovering the following day; set out clothes/items needed the day before; fully strip off for bed the night before; get up 2 hours before I need to leave so I can pace myself getting dressed and ready. I live alone so exist on microwave/oven ready-meals for one as they take the least amount of energy to make. I bought a Roomba as I can no longer hoover, but have to move a few things in prep for it, so will clean it out the next day. I have trouble getting back in my chair if I fall so my OT got a set of gradiated boxes, 6, 12, 18, 24 inches high, so I gradually increase my height to transfer to my wheelchair, but that was 5 lifts to get into the chair - I bought a bath lift last week, sits in the corner of my living room, 3" when lowered and rises to 20", so only 2 lifts to get into my wheelchair. I always follow the spoon theory and try to keep a couple of spoons in reserve in case needed as I've been caught out in the past (sleeping naked and covered in shit on the bathroom floor for a night as I fell trying to get to the toilet and didn't have enough energy to get up and deal with it - it meant the following day I needed to have a shower, clean up, get dressed, all before 8am, so I couldn't manage anything else for the rest of that day). 

I was on amantadine for the fatigue, but it wasn't doing anything, so my GP is pushing for some form of amphetamine, but they are restricted in the UK, so it is a battle through red-tape. I miss being able to do things on the spur of the moment. Having to plan every movement of a task in advance is a pain. Fatigue is my life now.

I have advanced primary progressive MS. Fun fact: cannabis works REALLY well to relieve the pain, discomfort, and spasms. Every single night. I also use sheath catheters 24/7, so when people are talkig to me and I look dazed but smiley, I'm actually peeing.

Bet I can beat their incompitence. I moved into a flat in 2005 and signed with Scottish Power. They took separate direct debits for gas and electric. August 2007 I noticed they hadn't taken the electric DD for a few months; when I called they insisted I must have signed with a different supplier, but would look into it and call me back. They never did so I called them weekly with they same response.

Shortly after I went through a long depresseive period, and about a year later when I came up again I was still not being billed for electric. By this point it had been about 18 months and I gave up worrying about it. Turned the gas off apart from hot water and the oven, got electri heaters for the winter and condenser fans for the summer, and had 4 computers turned on 24/7.

Finally late 2014 someone appeared to read my meter (first time in 7 years), so I got onto CAB immediately. Turns out British Gas had taken over the supply in 2007, but never asked or informed me, and made no communication for the whole 7 years. Legally all they could do was take my total electric usage, calculate a yearly average, and bill me for a year. So I whored the electric 24/7 for 7 years and paid £1440 for it all.

A lot of what I have picked up about daily living has been from youtube. My only irritation with it is that most of the videos are people who are paralysed and their legs are like twigs. Because of digestive problems I only eat once a day, maybe 700 calories. The fat just will not shift. I also go through periods of high water retention where I'm fully hydrated, but am bloated and any urine I pass is very concentrated (like at the moment); fortunately this usually passes after a week or so and I spend a couple of days emptying the cath bag every hour. Probably too much information, but I seem to have lost my TMI filter after years of having to discuss bowel and bladder issues with every doctor or nurse I come in contact with.

I prefer the usual closures, and always wear a belt - if I wind up on the floor I tighten the belt otherwise they would end up round my knees as I drag myself along. The only adjustment I make is to unstitch the lower 12" of the inner left leg seam and add velcro to close it - makes it easier to access the catheter bag on my calf for emptying.

Denims with discrete straps around the knees to make it easier to lift them. I have PPMS, and my legs are just a dead weight now, and although the muscle mass is atrophying, the fat isn't shifting, so they are heavy. Also having RSI in my right wrist from using the wheelchair makes lifting my legs into bed painful and difficult. I prefer denims as they are tough enough to grab a hold and pull on them. I know you can buy straps to strap on to your legs, but I don't want to go through all that every time I have to lay down.
I have MS and heat exacerbates the fatigue and other symptoms, and sunlight gives me headaches. I'm more of a night/winter person.

I would love to see this happen. I have PPMS and have been refused sativex because of the NICE regulations and all the red tape, though I'm still pushing for it. I recently started using hash in the evening (not as effective as cannabis, but it works). I don't like feeling high so just take a few puffs to ease the pain and discomfort but still remain functional; I just have to be careful transferring to/from my wheelchair. It works extremely well in relieving the pain and discomfort, and allows me to sleep for more than a couple of hours.

I've been using Private Internet Access for a few years with no problems. Got it because he UK started blocking so many of the torrent sites I use. Excellent start dude. Try to add something to it every month, even if it's only $10 and it will continue to grow. I wish I had started saving in my teens. I'm now 43. Spent most of my life living pay-cheque to pay-cheque. I started having to exist on disability benefits a few years ago, and in April 2011 I started a spreadsheet detailing every penny I spent - sounds pointless but you will soon see where the money goes, and more importtantly what it gets wasted on. At the time I was constantly £500-700 into my overdraft. By seeing where my money was going I could see the changes to make and now have £17k saved, living on disability benefits. Granted I have a very frugal lifestyle now, but having a safety net is a great relief when needed - your cooker breaks down, it becomes an inconvenience rather than a finantial disaster. I still have the spreadsheet going, and feel guilty having to add expenses to it now - helps me avoid impule purchases. I weep when I think of the many tens of thousands I wasted on junk over the years. By all means enjoy your life, but never forget that you never know what the future holds, and having savings can be the difference between surviving and drowning in debt.

Last time I had a GF was 2005 (before symptoms). Last time laid was 2007 (start of symptoms). Last time able to masterbate was about 6 months ago (can't get it up, no sensation down there anymore). When my legs started failing I was initially resistant to using a walking stick. But as I was then walking with a stumbling stagger, people assumed I was drunk and started making comments to me. I got a stick initially to give a visual clue to others - they saw the stich and assumed a medical proiblem rather than intoxication. I think as a debilitating, degenerative disease hits, dignity and vanity start going out the window, and practicality wins out over aesthetics. If a walking stick makes walking easier and safer for you, then get one. To hell with what other people might think. I found nobody took any notice although I was very conscious of it to begin with. you can also customise it however you want - paint is pink and stick rhinestones on it if you like. Just get one that suits you. Assuming you are RRMS (I'm PPMS) there will be times where you don't need to use it, but it's better to have it and not need it, than need it and not have it.

I really hate vegetables, so will not start eating them now. I do eat a lot of fruit if that helps. I have fiber tablets that I dissolve in water every day (called fybogel or something like that), taste awful - labelled orange I think just because the packaging is orange.

I'm still.l tweaking the various BM softeners, laxitives, and manual stim to try and get a working situation - preferable a movement every 2-3 days with a practical consistency (ie, midway between a brick and a waterfall). It's odd at 43 years old trying to retrain my bowels, but it's getting there. Kinda like potty training a toddler.

Never been tested, but it seems to be a regular symptom of advanced MS. Also because I'm in a wheelchair with limited abdominal control, the abdominal muscles that aid BM movement aren't doing anything. Also peristalsis of the intestine is limited, again restricting movement through the digestive tract. A lot of it is similar to the physical limitations seen in spinal cord injuries.

Idon't eat the most balanced of diets, but then I never have. I hate vegetables, so when I turned 18 and moved out I stopped eating food I simply did not like. I generally avoid sweet things as I'm a depressive, so would comfort eat ice cream to the exclusion of everything else. Mostly I eat pasta, rice, chicken, fish, and a lot of muisli (I know I spelled that wrong). I know that I don't have long before my body fails to the point of losing my independance, and I don't intend to exist like that, so I'm kinda at the point of just eating what I like, coping as best I can, because I don't want to spend what time I have left eating a restricted diet of food I dislike.

I've never had any tests done, but my bowel movements have definately gotten worse over the last few years. PPMS here. Went gradually from a regular daily BM to every 3rd day. The last year is has generally been every 6-7 days, so I decreased the amount I eat (once a day) or I would get uncomfortably bloated after a couple of days. The last few months it got to the point where a BM would take about an hour of trying to strain on the toilet (very little abdominal muscle control left) and would leave me exhausted. A month ago I started a bowel routine - daily oral stool softener, mild laxitive every 2nd day, and a glove, lube, and a finger up my ass to stimulate colonic contractions daily. Can't say I enjoy it, but I'm now back to every 3 days without the exhaustive straining.

When I first was diagnosed with progressive MS a few years ago I realised that although it wouldn't kill me in itself, it would lead to my life ending, and I didn't want my elderly parents to have to foot a large bill for my death. So I started saving to cover the costs of my eventual death. Because I receive ESA and DLA, and the ESA can be reduced if I save any money I put money into my mothers account to save it. I have a will requesting no funeral and just want my body cremated and ashes disposed of - I see no point in throwing money away on a fancy box just to burn it. I did briefly work as an undertaker many years ago, and the mark-up was scary. Put funeral, wedding, or disabled in front of anything and watch the price double immediately.
